extracted.intended_audience: users and programmers of the PARI/GP calculator (mathematicians/number-theorists and script authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Usage and programming guidelines for PARI/GP: editing and readline integration, function/prototype syntax and flags, control statements and loop constructs, debugging commands, and detailed classification of runtime/error conditions. Geared to writing gp scripts and using the GP interactive calculator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readline keybindings and editing commands
rubrics_metrics.description: C- combinations act on characters, M- (Meta/Alt) operate on words; ordinary keys insert text, arrow keys move cursor; familiar Emacs bindings work (C-a/C-e, M-b/M-f, C-k, M-d, C-y, M-y, C- for undo, C-t/M-t transpose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meta key may be labelled Alt or show a black diamond; Esc can replace Meta. Use <Return> to send commands. Many movement commands available (Emacs-style and Vi-mode via M-C-j). Examples: C-k kills to end of line, M-d kills to end of word, C-y yanks, M-y rotates kill-ring. M-- gives numeric argument to next readline command (e.g. M-- C-k).

rubrics_metrics.name: .inputrc customization
rubrics_metrics.description: You can change default readline bindings by creating a .inputrc file in your home directory; gp respects conditional sections ($if Pari-GP ... $endif).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example lines: set show-all-if-ambiguous; "\C-h": backward-delete-char; "\e\C-h": backward-kill-word. Use C-x C-r to re-read the init file during a session. Be careful: some bindings like ( and [ may be bound to pari-matched-insert (electric parentheses) which can be toggled by passing numeric arguments (e.g. M--2()). If readline version outputs 8-bit characters for Alt/Meta, set convert-meta on and set output-meta off in .inputrc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command completion behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Hitting <TAB> completes words context-dependently: gp attempts only meaningful completions based on context (user names after ~, paths, default keywords after default(), member keywords after '.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only one completion is meaningful, gp completes and may append a comma (if completing a default) or parentheses (if completing a function name); pressing <TAB> again will show the function's argument list. Pressing <TAB> twice shows a list of possible completions. Examples: typing def<TAB>se<TAB>10 to get default(seriesprecision,10). M-h gives short help on the word under cursor; M-H yields extended help (may open a dvi previewer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional argument notation in GP function syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional arguments are shown between braces { } with a default value; the {} are not typed by the user and denote optional arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typing foo(x) is equivalent to foo(x,0) if flag default is 0. A missing optional argument can be signaled by a comma or closing parenthesis (foo(x,) uses default). When a function has several optional arguments they are filled in order; use the empty-arg trick foo(6,,1) to set a far argument while leaving intermediate ones default. A star after an optional argument ({x}*) means any number of such arguments may be provided (used for print routines). A function with no mandatory arguments can be invoked without parentheses (not recommended in scripts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Library (C) prototype mapping and mandatory arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: The GP function prototype is translated into a library function signature (GEN foo(GEN x, long fl = 0)). For library programming, all arguments are mandatory; default values are encoded (NULL pointers, -1, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the library, functions are implemented without variable-argument GP-style behavior; variants exist for different flag values. The manual includes = default tokens in prototypes to indicate how missing arguments map to library encodings. Refer to the User’s Guide to the PARI library for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flags: generic vs binary
rubrics_metrics.description: Flags are optional arguments that change a routine's default behavior. There are two kinds: generic (explicit values described individually) and binary (compact integer representing many 0/1 toggles using bit positions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary flags are annotated by listing the meaning of each bit (e.g., 1: p0, 2: p1, 4: p2...). Binary numeric flags are concise but error-prone and rigid; use them primarily in interactive gp for speed. Where available, mnemonics (strings) are provided as an alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mnemonics for binary flags
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary flags may be replaced by character strings of symbolic identifiers (mnemonics) corresponding to toggles; mnemonics can be negated by prefixing no or removing the prefix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mnemonics are grouped by punctuation; example: Binary digits of flags mean: 1 = Parametric, 2 = Recursive. Instead of using 1, one could use "Parametric; no Recursive" or simply "Parametric". C-style bit-or notation like "Parametric | no Recursive" is also accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pointer (&) arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Parameters prefixed with & in prototypes (foo(x, &e)) indicate the function may assign a value to e as a side-effect; when passing the argument, the & must be typed explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of version 2.11.1, these pointer arguments are optional for documented functions and therefore appear in brackets in prototypes (e.g., Z issquare(x, {&e})).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lexical scoping of loop variables
rubrics_metrics.description: In constructs like for (X = a,b, seq) the loop variable X is lexically scoped to the loop; modifying a same-named variable outside the loop remains unaffected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example caveat: n = 5; for (n = 1,10, if (something_nice(), break)); \ at this point n is 5. If seq modifies the loop index variable, the loop iterator is modified accordingly (demonstrated with n += 2 inside the loop).

rubrics_metrics.name: break({n = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrupts execution of current seq and exits from the n innermost enclosing loops within the current function call (or the top-level loop).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: n must be positive; if n exceeds the number of enclosing loops, all enclosing loops are exited.

rubrics_metrics.name: breakpoint() and break loop
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrupts the program and enters the break loop; program continues when the break loop is exited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: calling breakpoint() inside a function suspends execution and shows the break prompt where local variables can be inspected; type <Return> to continue or 'break' to return to gp. The break loop is useful for interactive debugging.

rubrics_metrics.name: dbg_down({n = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: In the break loop: go down n frames in the call stack (opposite of dbg_up).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to navigate stack frames while debugging to cancel prior dbg_up calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: dbg_err()
rubrics_metrics.description: In the break loop: return the error data of the current error, if any (same data as provided to iferr's E parameter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: iferr(1/(Mod(2,12019)^(6!)-1),E,Vec(E)) shows how dbg_err()/iferr present error vectors. Use Vec(dbg_err()) to inspect the error components.

rubrics_metrics.name: dbg_up({n = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: In the break loop: go up n frames to inspect parent function data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dbg_down to cancel a dbg_up call.

rubrics_metrics.name: dbg_x(A, {n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Prints the inner structure of A (complete if n omitted, or up to level n otherwise), useful for debugging; similar to \x but does not require A to be a history entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be used inside the break loop to inspect objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: for(X = a, b, seq)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate seq where X goes from a to b (nothing done if a > b); a and b must be in R. If b is +oo, loop must be broken explicitly by user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loop variable is lexically scoped. Use break/return to exit infinite loops. Example: for (n = 1, 10, n += 2; print(n)).

rubrics_metrics.name: forcomposite(n = a, {b}, seq)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate seq where n ranges over composite numbers between a and b (inclusive if composite). Nothing is done if a > b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omitting b runs through all composites ≥ a (infinite loop unless broken). The loop index is read-only inside seq (attempting to modify it errors). Example output: 4,6,8,9,10 for a=0..10.

rubrics_metrics.name: fordiv(n, X, seq)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate seq where X ranges through the divisors of n; accepts either integer n or a factorization matrix (output of factor(n)). Divisors of an integer are returned in increasing size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid storing all divisors, use a slower constant-space method (example FORDIV implementation uses factorback). Timing examples compare fordiv vs equivalent implementations; fordiv is significantly faster and memory-efficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: fordivfactored(n, X, seq)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate seq where X ranges over [d, factor(d)] for each divisor d of n; useful because it avoids refactoring each divisor when evaluating multiplicative functions on divisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts factorization matrix instead of n. Faster than fordiv when n is hard to factor; example timings show fordivfactored faster than repeated factor calls. Also forfactored wrapper avoids factoring many consecutive n's.

rubrics_metrics.name: forell(E, a, b, seq, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Iterate over elliptic curves of conductors from a to b: E = [name, M, G] where name is Cremona name, M minimal model, G Z-basis of free part of E(Q). If flag != 0 select only first curve in each isogeny class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires elldata database for specified conductors. Example: forell(E,1,500,c++); returns number of curves or isogeny classes depending on flag. Library syntax provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: forfactored(N = a, b, seq)
rubrics_metrics.description: Iterate where N is [n, factor(n)] and n goes from a to b (integers); implemented for |a|,|b| < 2^64 (2^32 on 32-bit machines). Uses a sieve on interval and is much faster than factoring each n separately when interval length large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timings given for various ranges show large speedups versus repeated factor calls. Performance depends on primelimit; function slows if primelimit < sqrt(b). Works best when b-a is large compared to primelimit.

rubrics_metrics.name: forpart(X = k, seq, {a = k}, {n = k})
rubrics_metrics.description: Iterate over partitions X of integer k (nondecreasing sequences summing to k). By default parts are positive; optional parameters n (length restrictions) and a (part size restrictions) allow filtering and zero-padding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parts returned as t_VECSMALL vectors in specific order (by increasing size, lexicographic within size). Examples show restricting number of parts and part sizes; behavior unspecified if X is modified inside the loop.

rubrics_metrics.name: forperm(a, p, seq)
rubrics_metrics.description: Iterate p over permutations: if a is integer, permutations of {1,..,a} in lexicographic order; if a is a vector, iterate multipermutations lexicographically ≥ a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show lexicographic ordering of generated permutations or multipermutations.

rubrics_metrics.name: forprime(p = a, {b}, seq)
rubrics_metrics.description: Iterate p over prime numbers between real a and b, incrementing p to nextprime(p+1) each iteration. Nothing is done if a > b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting b to +oo runs over all primes ≥ a (infinite loop unless user breaks). The loop index p is read-only inside seq (attempt to modify errors).

rubrics_metrics.name: forprimestep(p = a, b, q, seq)
rubrics_metrics.description: Iterate p over primes in an arithmetic progression in [a,b]: q is integer modulus (p ≡ a mod q) or an intmod restricting to a congruence class. Nothing is done if a > b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If b = +oo runs indefinitely. Current implementation restricts modulus to unsigned long (64 or 32 bits). p is read-only inside seq; overflow of modulus triggers an error.

rubrics_metrics.name: forsquarefree(N = a, b, seq)
rubrics_metrics.description: Iterate N = [n, factor(n)] where n runs over squarefree integers between integers a and b (same sign). Nothing done if a > b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only implemented for |a|,|b| < 2^64 (2^32 on 32-bit). Uses a sieve and is much faster than factoring each n; runs in time O(...). Example timings show speed advantage relative to forfactored and factor. Note: set of fundamental discriminants can be enumerated with this loop but they may not be in order.

rubrics_metrics.name: forstep(X = a, b, s, seq)
rubrics_metrics.description: Iterate X from a to b in increments of s; s can be a real step, an intmod (arithmetic progression), or a vector of successive steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing done when step sign incompatible with bounds (s > 0 and a > b, etc.). b = +oo yields an infinite loop unless broken. Examples show integer step, Mod step, and vector steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: forsubgroup(H = G, {bound}, seq)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate seq for each subgroup H of abelian group G (SNF form or list of elementary divisors). If bound is present restrict output to subgroups of index less than bound or exactly a given index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subgroups are not ordered obviously (except for p-groups). A subgroup is returned as a generator matrix whose columns give its generators. For maximal speed output is algorithmic; use mathnf(concat(G,H)) to canonicalize subgroups. Intended for huge groups where enumerating all subgroups would be massive.

rubrics_metrics.name: forsubset(nk, s, seq)
rubrics_metrics.description: If nk is integer n, iterate s over all subsets of {1,..,n}; if nk is [n,k], iterate subsets of size k. Order: lexicographic among subsets of same size; smaller subsets come first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Running time proportional to number of subsets (2^n or binomial(n,k)). Examples and timings given (e.g., binomial(40,35)).

rubrics_metrics.name: forvec(X = v, seq, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Let v be n-component vector of two-component ranges [ai,bi]; X varies over the n-dimensional hyperrectangle with lexicographic ordering; type of X matches v (t_VEC or t_COL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag=1 generate only nondecreasing vectors X; flag=2 strictly increasing. Example: forvec (X=[[0,1],[-1,1]], print(X)).

rubrics_metrics.name: if(a, {seq1}, {seq2})
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate seq1 if a is non-zero, otherwise seq2; seq1 or seq2 may be empty. The value of an if expression is the value of the branch evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may omit the second comma when only seq1 is desired. Compound ifs can be chained to emulate switch/case. Boolean operators && and || short-circuit when determining truth value. Note: break/next operate on loops only; if is not a loop.

rubrics_metrics.name: iferr(seq1, E, seq2, {pred})
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate seq1; if an error occurs set the formal parameter E to the error data and, if pred absent or true, catch the error and evaluate seq2. The return value is seq1 if no error, else seq2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: seq2 and pred can reference E; code in seq2 should verify the error is expected (errname(E)). The error can be rethrown using error(E). Example: using iferr to implement ECM factoring where certain errors trigger returning gcd of component(E,2) with N. Use dbg_err() in break loop to inspect current error data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal error: "e ARCH"
rubrics_metrics.description: A requested feature s is not available on this architecture or operating system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component (t_STR): the missing feature name s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal error: "e BUG"
rubrics_metrics.description: A bug in the PARI library, in function s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component (t_STR): the function name s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal error: "e FILE"
rubrics_metrics.description: Error while trying to open a file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has two components: 1 (t_STR) the file type (input, output, etc.), 2 (t_STR) the file name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal error: "e IMPL"
rubrics_metrics.description: A requested feature s is not implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component (t_STR): the feature name s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal error: "e PACKAGE"
rubrics_metrics.description: Missing optional package s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component (t_STR): the package name s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syntax/dimension error: "e DIM"
rubrics_metrics.description: The dimensions of arguments x and y submitted to function s do not match (e.g., matrix dimension mismatch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has three components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2 offending argument x, 3 offending argument y.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag error: "e FLAG"
rubrics_metrics.description: A flag argument is out of bounds in function s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component (t_STR): the function name s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not-a-function error: "e NOTFUNC"
rubrics_metrics.description: Generated by the evaluator when trying to call a GEN x which is not a t_CLOSURE (e.g. f = 1; f(2);).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component: the offending GEN x.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operation error: "e OP"
rubrics_metrics.description: Impossible operation between two objects that cannot be typecast to a sensible common domain for deeper reasons than a type mismatch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has three components: 1 (t_STR) operator name op; 2 first argument; 3 second argument. Example: O(2)+O(3) or incompatible p-adic additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type error: "e TYPE"
rubrics_metrics.description: An argument x of function s had an unexpected type (e.g., factor("blah")).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has two components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2 the offending argument x.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type mismatch error: "e TYPE2"
rubrics_metrics.description: Forbidden operation between two objects that cannot be typecast to a common domain because their types do not match (e.g., Mod(1,2) + Pi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has three components: 1 (t_STR) operator name op, 2 first argument, 3 second argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority error: "e PRIORITY"
rubrics_metrics.description: Object o in function s contains variables whose priority is incompatible with expected operation (e.g., creating a polynomial whose coefficients have higher-priority variables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has four components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2 offending argument o, 3 (t_STR) operator op describing priority error, 4 (t_POL) variable v describing priority error. The argument satisfies variable(x) op variable(v).

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable mismatch error: "e VAR"
rubrics_metrics.description: The variables of arguments x and y submitted to function s do not match up (e.g., Mod(t,t^2+1) inside nfinit(x^2+1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has three components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2 (t_POL) argument x, 3 (t_POL) argument y.

rubrics_metrics.name: Component access error: "e COMPONENT"
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempt to access a non-existent component of a vector/matrix/list: index out of allowed range (<1 or >allowed length).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has four components: 1 (t_STR) function name, 2 (t_STR) operator op (< or >), 3 (t_GEN) numerical limit l, 4 (GEN) the index x. It satisfies x op l.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain error: "e DOMAIN"
rubrics_metrics.description: An argument is not in the function's domain (numeric or other bounds violated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has five components: 1 (t_STR) function name, 2 (t_STR) mathematical name of out-of-domain argument, 3 (t_STR) operator op describing domain error, 4 (t_GEN) numerical limit l, 5 (GEN) the out-of-domain argument x (satisfies x op l).

rubrics_metrics.name: Max prime list overflow: "e MAXPRIME"
rubrics_metrics.description: A function using the precomputed list of prime numbers ran out of primes (requested prime bound overran primelimit or is 0/unknown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component: 1 (t_INT) the requested prime bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory allocation error: "e MEM"
rubrics_metrics.description: A call to pari_malloc or pari_realloc failed (out of memory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has no component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation overflow: "e OVERFLOW"
rubrics_metrics.description: An object in function s becomes too large to be represented within PARI's hardcoded limits (e.g., extremely large tower exponentials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component (t_STR): the function name s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision error: "e PREC"
rubrics_metrics.description: Function s fails because input accuracy is too low (default accuracy issue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component (t_STR): the function name s. Example: floor(1e100) failing at default accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stack overflow: "e STACK"
rubrics_metrics.description: The PARI stack overflows during execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has no component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alarm/timeout error: "e ALARM"
rubrics_metrics.description: A timeout generated by the alarm function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component (t_STR): the error message to print.

rubrics_metrics.name: User-triggered error: "e USER"
rubrics_metrics.description: A user error as triggered by error(g1, ..., gn).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component (t_VEC): the vector of n arguments given to error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical error: "e CONSTPOL"
rubrics_metrics.description: An argument of function s is a constant polynomial, which does not make sense for that function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component (t_STR): the function name s. Example: galoisinit(Pol(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical error: "e COPRIME"
rubrics_metrics.description: Function s expected coprime arguments but received x,y which were not coprime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has three components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2 argument x, 3 argument y.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical error: "e INV"
rubrics_metrics.description: Tried to invert a non-invertible object x in function s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has two components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2 the non-invertible x. If x = Mod(a,b) and a not 0 mod b, this indicates gcd(a,b) may reveal a non-trivial factor of modulus b.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical error: "e IRREDPOL"
rubrics_metrics.description: Function s expected an irreducible polynomial but received a reducible one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has two components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2 (t_POL) the offending polynomial. Example: nfinit(x^2-1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic math error: "e MISC"
rubrics_metrics.description: A generic uncategorized error with a message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component (t_STR): the error message to print.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modulus inconsistency: "e MODULUS"
rubrics_metrics.description: Moduli x and y submitted to function s are inconsistent (incompatible modulus contexts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has three components: 1 (t_STR) function s, 2 argument x, 3 argument y. Example: nfalgtobasis(nfinit(t^3-2), Mod(t,t^2+1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primality expectation error: "e PRIME"
rubrics_metrics.description: Function s expected a prime number and received p which was not prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has two components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2 the argument p. Example: idealprimedec(nf,4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero-polynomial roots error: "e ROOTS0"
rubrics_metrics.description: An argument of function s is the zero polynomial and roots are needed (e.g., polroots(0)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has one component (t_STR): the function name s.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nth-root error: "e SQRTN"
rubrics_metrics.description: Trying to compute an n-th root of x which does not exist in the given context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E has two components: 1 (t_STR) function name s, 2 the argument x. Example: sqrt(Mod(-1,3)).
